Mussolini invaded Greece in October 1940 and lost. Six months later Germany did the same job in three weeks.

The Axis invasion of Greece, 1941 — a thread 🧵🗺️

1/ Italy attacked from Albania on 28 October 1940, expecting a walkover. The Greeks held, counterattacked, and by winter occupied a strip of Albania. It was the first land defeat of an Axis power in the war — and it dragged Berlin in.

2/ Germany struck on 6 April 1941, hitting Greece and Yugoslavia together. Greek defences faced the wrong way: the fortified Metaxas Line guarded the Bulgarian border, so German columns drove through collapsing Yugoslavia and came in behind it.

3/ Thessaloniki fell on 9 April, three days in, and the Greek army in Eastern Macedonia surrendered with it. Bulgaria's zone appears in the northeast almost at once — Sofia had joined the Axis in March and was paid in Greek territory.

4/ The Army of Epirus — the force that had beaten Italy — surrendered on 20 April, cut off from behind. The king and government left for Crete on 23 April. German troops entered Athens on 27 April, and the mainland was done by the end of the month.

5/ The British and Commonwealth force sent to help evacuated by sea, roughly 50,000 men, abandoning most of its heavy equipment. Greece was then split three ways: Bulgaria in the northeast, Italy across most of the rest, Germany holding the strategic points.
6/ Crete came in May: a German airborne assault that worked, and cost so many paratroopers doing it that Hitler never authorised a large airborne operation again.

7/ The occupation's worst damage was not military. Requisitioning and blockade produced a famine in the winter of 1941–42 that killed an estimated 300,000 people in a country of roughly 7 million.
